theme: published research recommendations and project priorities
question: Which recommendations and research agendas from Indus archaeology, epigraphy and computation can this project act on with current evidence?
outcome: A live-web exploratory survey records 33 rows from 31 source records across data/corpora, context/chronology, linguistic approaches, computation, collaboration/access, and excavation/science. Corpus curation joined to chronology and context is a recurring methodological agenda. The Frenez lecture title was identified, but transcript, date, venue details and timestamps remain unavailable; its four lecture-specific rows rely on the user's summary.
challenge: YouTube watch and timed-text retrieval were throttled. Several requested researchers had only snippet, abstract or citation-level source access; their source/page locators remain to be verified. Literature discovery preceded the protocol, so the coded survey is exploratory.
remedy: Preserved source access labels and search gaps; distinguished the user's lecture summary from checked publications; reused the October 2 dataset landscape, context plan and relevant registry entries; supplied a reproducible CSV export script.
retry_when: A transcript or event page becomes accessible; primary sources can be opened to verify all page locators; or a reviewer identifies additional published agendas or disputes. Add a dated source-verification extension rather than overwriting this exploratory survey.
